comment: The FIFTH typecheck pass. Covers the two trees the other four leave completely unchecked: the `tests/` suite (minus `tests/react/`, which tsconfig.react.test.json already owns because it needs react-jsx) and the package-root tooling files (vite.config.*.ts, vitest.config.ts, playwright.*.config.ts, vitest.shims.d.ts). Before this pass existed, `nx typecheck ui` read 548 of the 677 .ts/.tsx files in the package: tsconfig.json includes only `src/**`, tsconfig.react.json only `frameworks/**`, tsconfig.react.test.json only `tests/react/**`, tsconfig.mcp.json only `src/agent-tooling/mcp/**` — so a type error anywhere else shipped green. Strictness is deliberately the same as tsconfig.json (strict + isolatedModules); the JSX config is Solid's, matching the suite. DO NOT relax these options to make the pass green — quarantine a file in `exclude` with a reason instead, so the gap stays visible.

quarantine.why: Turning this pass on surfaced 36 pre-existing errors in 9 files — exactly what it was built to find. 12 of them were one dead file (tests/animated-logo.tsx), now deleted. The remaining 24 are quarantined here rather than papered over with looser compilerOptions, because most need a src-side fix or a call about intent, not a cast in the test. Delete an entry and fix the file; do not add entries without a line here saying what broke.
quarantine.tests/components/message.test.tsx: 4 errors. Real API drift, not test noise. `<Message role="user">` typechecks against JSX.HTMLAttributes, so `role` is the ARIA attribute and 'user' is not a valid ARIA role — the test puts an invalid role on a div. `<MessageAvatar fallback="AI" />` fails because MessageAvatarProps marks `src`/`alt` required even though the component's whole point is rendering `fallback` when `src` is absent. Both fixes land in src/components/message.tsx.
quarantine.tests/primitives/card-recovery.test.ts: 9 errors, all TS2722 'cannot invoke possibly undefined'. dismissRecovery() returns Pick<CardPolicy,'onDismiss'|'onReopen'>, and Pick preserves CardPolicy's `?`, so the return type says the handlers may be missing when the implementation always returns both. The honest fix is the return type in src/primitives/card-recovery.ts, not `!` in the test.
quarantine.tests/remote/host-embed.test.ts: 1 error. The test asserts a 'render-error' fault code that is no longer a member of WireFaultCode. Needs a call on whether the code was dropped or renamed.
quarantine.tests/scripts/display-name.test.ts: 1 error, TS7016. Imports ../../scripts/_ts-helpers.mjs, which has no declarations. Needs either allowJs on this pass or a .d.mts beside the helper.
quarantine.tests/stories/element-controls.test.ts: 2 errors, TS2571. Unnarrowed `unknown` from a JSON/dynamic read. Mechanical.
quarantine.vite.config.ts: 3 errors. `import type { OutputBundle, OutputChunk } from 'vite'` — vite declares those locally and does not re-export them, so the import is broken today and `chunk` degrades to unknown. Same bug in vite.config.elements.ts.
quarantine.vite.config.elements.ts: 3 errors. Same broken OutputBundle/OutputChunk type import as vite.config.ts.
quarantine.vitest.config.ts: 1 error. The storybook browser project passes `launchOptions` inside a browser `instances[]` entry, and BrowserInstanceOption in the installed @vitest/browser-playwright does not declare it. Worth checking whether the CI chromium hardening flags (--disable-dev-shm-usage, --no-sandbox, the memory cap) are actually reaching the browser or being dropped.

notAlsoCovered..storybook/**: Left out on purpose. .storybook/preview.ts imports ../dist/kai.es.js — a gitignored build artifact — so the file cannot typecheck before a build, and `nx typecheck ui` must not require one. (For the record, a probe over the three files reports 2 errors: that missing-module import, plus API_HashEntry.title in manager.ts.)
notAlsoCovered.src/elements/resizable.d.ts: FIXED — renamed to src/elements/resizable.globals.d.ts, which puts it in the src pass for the first time. It was unreachable because TypeScript drops a .d.ts when a same-named .ts/.tsx sits beside it, and resizable.tsx does. The rename makes the HTMLElementEventMap half work (measured: `el.addEventListener('kai-maximize-intent', e => e.detail)` was TS2339 before and narrows correctly after). It does NOT fix the HTMLElementTagNameMap half, which loses to the generated element-types.d.ts — see that file's header. Note also that no pass CHECKS a .d.ts body: every one sets skipLibCheck, so being in the program makes the augmentation take effect, not get verified.
